<section class="section prospective-section">
# Prospective researchers

I welcome enquiries from prospective researchers interested in questions about meaning and cognition. I am particularly interested in projects that connect questions about linguistic representation with questions about composition, inference, memory, knowledge, or the processes involved in comprehension.

Projects need not fall neatly within one of my current research programmes. What matters more is a clear theoretical question, a good fit with my expertise, and a willingness to use linguistic theory and empirical evidence to constrain one another.

If you are considering working with me, the [Research](research/index.html) page is the best indication of the kinds of questions that currently interest me.

## Graduate research

I supervise research projects for students on Oxford's **DPhil, MPhil, and MSt (Research Preparation) in Linguistics, Philology and Phonetics** programmes. Prospective students are welcome to contact me before applying. You do not need to send a fully developed research proposal in an initial email; a short description of the problem you are interested in, why you think it connects with my research, and your relevant background is much more useful.

Formal admissions requirements, deadlines and funding arrangements are handled by the University and Faculty. Please consult the Oxford graduate admissions pages for current information.

## Postdoctoral researchers

I am happy to discuss postdoctoral projects that fit closely with my research programme, including applications for external fellowships hosted at Oxford. If you are considering developing a fellowship proposal with me, please get in touch well in advance of the deadline: good proposals benefit from time to develop the research questions and intellectual fit together.

Funded postdoctoral positions attached to particular projects, when available, will be advertised formally.

## Undergraduate research

I also supervise undergraduate research projects in language and cognition. Within Linguistics, **Paper C** provides an opportunity to pursue an independent research project, and I supervise projects where the question and my expertise are a good fit. I also supervise **Extended Projects for fourth-year Experimental Psychology and PPL students**, with project allocation organised annually through Experimental Psychology.

If you are an Oxford undergraduate considering an independent project, the most useful starting point is a research question rather than a fully worked-out experiment. I am happy to discuss how a promising question might be developed into a feasible project.

## Getting in touch

If you are contacting me about prospective research, a brief email is best. Tell me the question or problem that interests you, how you see it connecting with my research, and a little about your relevant background. A CV is useful; a long research proposal is not necessary for an initial enquiry.
</section>
